# EnterpriseGlue v0.34.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.33.0`.

## Highlights

- **documentation:** Requires central account proof for automatic customer documentation domain admission.
- **documentation:** Adds private customer documentation workspaces with verified-domain or individual-reader admission, checked on every protected request.

## User and administrator impact

- Verified-domain customer workspaces admit only centrally verified Cloud account sessions. Tenant-provider email assertions alone no longer authorize domain-based access. Individual-reader policies retain their immutable-account restrictions.
- Publishers can admit verified accounts at exact approved email domains automatically, or require additional expiring individual grants.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Install the corrected account service before enabling verified-domain customer documentation bundles.
- Roll out the account contract before enabling customer documentation bundles.

## API and integration compatibility

- Configuration, session and workspace-discovery responses advertise customer-documentation/v2. The matching gateway requires this central domain-authority contract on every customer read; older account responses fail closed.
- Adds customer workspace discovery, scoped session authorization and workspaceContract capability metadata for deployment preflight.

## Configuration

- No policy schema change. The publisher-selected verified_domain mode requires the persisted central cloud_account session class; explicit_readers remains unchanged.
- Adds optional private EG_DOCUMENTATION_WORKSPACES_JSON. accessMode verified_domain admits current verified exact-domain accounts without individual grants; the default explicit_readers mode retains individual expiry checks. Both default to no configured workspaces. Policy changes require rollout to every runtime instance.

## Database migrations

- Reuses the existing persisted source session class. No database migration.
- Reuses existing verified accounts and exact session rows; no tenants or grants are inferred from application memberships.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- A tenant-controlled identity provider cannot establish customer email-domain authority merely by asserting an allowed email or verified-email claim.
- The v2 account contract prevents older account service instances from authorizing customer reads during rollout or rollback.
- General documentation access never authorizes customer content.
- Every asset rechecks the current verified email, account, source session and exact configured workspace domain. Domain admission must be explicitly selected; legacy policies retain individual-reader restrictions.

## Known limitations

- Real corporate sign-in and deployed account/gateway isolation still require acceptance before customer content publication.
- The admission policy is publisher-managed deployment configuration. There is no grant administration UI or automatic upstream AD group provisioning.
- Existing upstream account revocation and directory reconciliation determine when upstream AD changes become locally visible.

## Rollback

- Disable customer bundles before rolling back the corrected account contract; the matching gateway rejects responses that lack the v2 contract.
- Remove customer bundles before rolling back the account contract. An older account response cannot authorize a customer-scoped read.

## Validation evidence

- Local auth routes and domain-authority regressions: 16 files and 197 tests passed.
- Exact account/gateway HTTP qualification with owned PostgreSQL: 2 files and 3 tests passed.
- Backend/shared build, backend typecheck and affected lint passed. No deployed or customer-content publication acceptance is claimed.
- Local auth routes: 15 files and 195 tests passed, including verified-domain admission, other-domain/subdomain denial, unverified/disabled users, policy removal and legacy individual-grant compatibility.
- Exact gateway/account HTTP qualification with owned PostgreSQL: 2 files and 3 tests passed, including both customers and protected pages, search, downloads, JavaScript and receipts.
- Backend host/shared build, backend TypeScript check and affected lint passed. Portal compilation/browser, publication and infrastructure gates are recorded separately in their owning repositories.
- No hosted CI, live rollout or customer-content publication is claimed by this local evidence.
